title: Adds tags to ggpot2 facets
text: default usage, can simply add tag_facets() add tag panel ggplo2 plot. want tag rows columns instead panel indivdually, can set tag argument.
code: library(tagger) library(ggplot2)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +    geom_point() +    facet_grid(cyl ~ vs) +    tag_facets() ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +    geom_point() +    facet_grid(cyl ~ vs) +    tag_facets(tag = "rc")

title: Get labels assigned to each panel of a tagged plot — get_layout
code: library(ggplot2) g <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   facet_grid(cyl ~ vs) +   tag_facets("rc")  # By default these functions retrieve tags from # the result of ggplo2::last_plot().  # Get all tags get_layout() #>   PANEL ROW COL cyl vs COORD TAG_ROW TAG_COL TAG_PANEL #> 1     1   1   1   4  0     1       a       1       a.1 #> 2     2   1   2   4  1     1       a       2       a.2 #> 3     3   2   1   6  0     1       b       1       b.1 #> 4     4   2   2   6  1     1       b       2       b.2 #> 5     5   3   1   8  0     1       c       1       c.1 #> 6     6   3   2   8  1     1       c       2       c.2  # Get one tag get_tag(cyl == 4 & vs == 0) #> [1] "a.1"  # Get more than one tag get_tag(cyl == 4, n = 2) #> [1] "a.1" "a.2"   get_row(cyl == 4) #> [1] "a" get_col(vs == 0) #> [1] 1  # Use it with inline markdown to refer always to the correct panel: # "As you can see in panel `r get_tag(cyl == 4 & vs == 0)` ..."

title: Adds tags to facets — tag_facets
code: tag_facets(   tag = c("panel", "rc", "cr"),   position = "tl",   tag_levels = c("a", "1"),   tag_pool = NULL,   tag_prefix = "",   tag_suffix = ")",   tag_sep = ".",   clip = "on" )

title: Adds tags to facets — tag_facets
text: tag Character indicating element tag. Possible values "panel": single panels individually tag. "rc": facets tagged row column. "cr": facets tagged columns row. position Character indicating position tag. Options "tl" (top-left), "tr" (top-right), "br" (bottom-right) "bl" (bottom-left). Alternatively, finer control, can list elements "x", "y", "hjust" "vjust" define position tag within panel. tag_levels character vector defining enumeration format use level. Possible values '' lowercase letters, '' uppercase letters, '1' numbers, '' lowercase Roman numerals, '' uppercase Roman numerals. can also list containing character vectors defining arbitrary tag sequences. element list scalar one '', '', '1', ', '', level expanded expected sequence. tag_pool optional character vector user-defined "pool" tags. NULL, used instead tag_levels. least long total number panels. tag_prefix, tag_suffix Strings appear tag. tag_sep separator different tag levels clip drawing clipped extent plot panel? clip set "" (default), tags drawn outside plotting area. Set clip "" draw tags anywhere.

title: Adds tags to facets — tag_facets
text: Tags inherit aesthetic properties (size, font, colour, etc...) strip.text strip.background defined ggplot2::theme(). fine-grained detail, can overridden setting tagger.panel.tag.text tagger.panel.tag.background.

title: Adds tags to facets — tag_facets
code: library(ggplot2) # Base plot g <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   facet_grid(cyl ~ vs)  g + tag_facets()  g + tag_facets("rc")  g + tag_facets("cr")  g + tag_facets(position = "br")  g + tag_facets("rc", tag_levels  = c("A", "I"))   # You can get finer control over position. g + tag_facets(position = list(x = 0.5, y = 0.5))   # Draw tags inside the panel strip with clip = "off" and custom position. g +   facet_wrap(cyl ~ vs) +   tag_facets(position = list(x = 0, y = 1, vjust = 0, hjust = 0), clip = "off")   g + tag_facets(tag_pool = c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"), tag_suffix = "")  # Thanks to theme inheritance, tags should look acceptable # out of the box in any theme. g + tag_facets() +    theme_dark()   # But you can control their appearance and create your own atrocities g + tag_facets() +    theme_dark() +    theme(tagger.panel.tag.text = element_text(color = "red", size = 16),          tagger.panel.tag.background = element_rect(fill = "purple"))
